sample-plants-gr3.title: Plant Parts
sample-plants-gr3.subject: science
sample-plants-gr3.shows: grade 3 science: label a plant, circle, a sentence
sample-plants-gr3.instructions: Write your number in the boxes. Spelling doesn't count unless it says so.

questions.prompt: Label the parts of the plant.
questions.picture: A simple plant: a flower on top, a stem, two leaves, a ground line, and roots under the ground. Box 1 points to the flower, box 2 to a leaf, box 3 to the stem, box 4 to the roots.

questions.prompt: What do the roots do for the plant?
questions.key: Roots take in (soak up, drink) water from the soil, and/or hold the plant in the ground. Either idea earns full credit.

questions.prompt: What does a plant need to make its food?

options.why: Yes! Leaves use sunlight to make food.
Soil gives water, but the leaves make the food.
Plants need light to make food.

sample-fractions-gr5.title: Exit Ticket: Adding Fractions
sample-fractions-gr5.subject: math
sample-fractions-gr5.shows: grade 5 math: shade fraction strips, a word problem
sample-fractions-gr5.instructions: Write your ID number in the boxes, not your name. Show your work.

questions.prompt: Strip Sum: The top strip shows 1/3 and the middle strip shows 1/4. Shade the bottom strip to show 1/3 + 1/4. Then write the sum.

checklist.item: Exactly 7 of the 12 parts in the bottom strip are shaded (usually 4 for 1/3, then 3 for 1/4).
The sum written after the = sign is 7/12.

questions.picture: Three fraction strips of the same length, stacked. Top strip: 3 equal parts with 1 shaded, labeled 1/3 on the left. Middle strip: 4 equal parts with 1 shaded, labeled 1/4 on the left. Bottom strip: 12 equal parts with none shaded, labeled 1/3 + 1/4 on the left, and '= ________' printed to its right for the sum.

questions.prompt: Walk to the Library: Rosa walks 1/2 mile to the park. Then she walks 3/5 mile to the library. How far does she walk in all?
questions.key: Rewrites both fractions with a common denominator of 10 (5/10 + 6/10) and adds to get 11/10, which is 1 1/10 miles. 11/10 or 1 1/10 is full credit. The mistake to look for: adding the tops and the bottoms to get 4/7.

questions.prompt: Spot the Sum: Which one equals 1/2 + 1/3? Circle the letter.

options.why: That adds tops and bottoms. 2/5 is less than 1/2, so it's too small.
Yes: 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6, so the sum is 5/6.
Sixths plus sixths are still sixths. Keep 6 as the denominator.

sample-ratios-gr6.title: Smoothie Stand Ratios
sample-ratios-gr6.subject: math
sample-ratios-gr6.shows: grade 6 math: a table, show-your-work math, a graph, a choice
sample-ratios-gr6.instructions: Show your work where there's room. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.prompt: Recipe Ratio: A smoothie uses 2 cups of mango for every 3 cups of yogurt. Fill in the table.
Unit Price: 6 smoothies cost $15. How much does 1 smoothie cost?
questions.key: Divides 15 by 6 (or finds the cost of 2 then halves, or a tape diagram) to get 2.50 dollars per smoothie.

questions.prompt: Plot It: Plot three points from the table, (2, 3), (4, 6), and (8, 12), as mango and yogurt cups. Connect them with a line.

checklist.item: A straight line connects the points (and may extend through the origin).

questions.picture: A coordinate grid, first quadrant, x from 0 to 10 (mango, cups) and y from 0 to 12 (yogurt, cups), grid lines every 1 unit, labels every 2.

questions.prompt: Same Taste? Which recipe tastes the same as 2 cups mango to 3 cups yogurt?

options.why: Adding the same amount changes the ratio.
1:2 has more yogurt for each cup of mango.

sample-spanish-gr9.title: En mi casa
sample-spanish-gr9.subject: Spanish
sample-spanish-gr9.shows: grade 9 Spanish: vocabulary, accents count, a short paragraph
sample-spanish-gr9.instructions: Escribe tu número de ID, no tu nombre. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.prompt: Completa con la forma correcta del verbo (spelling and accents count).
questions.text: Yo {1} (comer) en la cocina. Mi hermana {2} (estudiar) en su cuarto. Nosotros {3} (ver) la televisión en la sala.

questions.prompt: Match each room to what you do there. Write the letter in the box.
Describe tu cuarto en dos oraciones. (Describe your room in two sentences.)

rubric.criterion: Two complete sentences in Spanish about a room.
Verbs and adjectives agree (e.g. 'mi cuarto es pequeño', 'hay dos ventanas').
Uses at least two vocabulary words from the unit (cama, ventana, escritorio, lámpara, etc.).

questions.prompt: ¿Dónde está la lámpara? 'The lamp is next to the bed.'

options.text: La lámpara está debajo de la cama.
La lámpara está encima de la cama.
options.why: Encima de means on top of.

options.text: La lámpara está al lado de la cama.
options.why: ¡Sí! Al lado de means next to.

options.text: La lámpara está lejos de la cama.
